_comment: RenderForge tool registry. 'status' vocabulary: verified-here (I ran it on real data in this workspace) | verified-synthetic (ran on data I generated) | verified-prior (the user's earlier projects show it working; evidence path given, not re-run) | installed (present locally, not exercised) | candidate (not installed, plausible) | reference (read-only reference) | rejected. GitHub license/last-push/release are merged from github_meta.json via 'repo'.

layers.capture: L0 Acquire GPU / frame data from a running game
layers.ingest: L1 Turn a capture into the neutral Extract Package
layers.source: L2 Read the game's own asset files (pak / bundle / VFS)
layers.match: L3 Reconcile captured data with source assets
layers.emit: L5 Write scene into a target engine / DCC
layers.control: L6 Drive the target editor interactively (MCP / scripting)
layers.validate: L7 Render and compare against the reference frame
layers.orchestrate: L8 Registry, game profiles, recipes, planner, skills

tools.name: RenderDoc
evidence: workspace/wuwa_bridge (2.0GB D3D11 capture -> 19k instances)
renderforge/rd_scripts/rf_extract.py
tools.notes: Installed 1.45; upstream is at v1.46. Python API is the batch extraction workhorse. Cannot capture titles whose anti-cheat blocks DLL injection (commonly reported for HoYo titles; not tested here) - use the 3DMigoto route for those.
risks: anti-cheat blocks injection in many online games
1.45 vs mcp-bundled 1.43 runtime mismatch only matters for the MCP

tools.name: RenderDoc MCP (JiaboLi)
evidence: tools/renderdoc-mcp (v0.3.0 binaries): opened 590MB capture, list_draws=166, get_pipeline_state
.mcp.json
tools.notes: Best for interactive Q&A about a frame. v0.3.1 has no Windows binary release (source only, needs build against RenderDoc source); v0.3.0 binary bundles RenderDoc 1.43. Bulk extraction is faster/more complete via our own rd_extract script (vertex SRVs, instancing, cbuffers).
risks: bundled RenderDoc runtime older than installed

tools.name: RenderDoc contrib extensions
tools.notes: Community UI extensions; useful as examples of the extension API. Not needed for headless extraction.

tools.name: NVIDIA Nsight Graphics
tools.notes: Fallback when RenderDoc cannot capture (e.g. DX12 + ray tracing). No known scripted resource export comparable to RenderDoc's Python API, so treat as visual/shader debugging, not as an extraction source.

tools.name: PIX on Windows
tools.notes: D3D12-only fallback for titles RenderDoc mishandles. Same caveat as Nsight: export automation unverified.

tools.name: 3DMigoto (Frame Analysis)
engines: any D3D11 (used for Unity/UE anime games)
evidence: a local 3DMigoto FrameAnalysis dump (1.9 GB)
workspace/zzz_frame01 (ingested here)
tools.notes: Capture mechanism behind GIMI/SRMI/ZZMI/WWMI. A Frame Analysis dump contains PRE-vertex-shader buffers (no post-VS clip positions) so the generic transform solver does not apply; ingest emits model-space meshes and needs a per-game placement hook.
risks: licence not asserted by GitHub API - check before redistributing
injection may violate a game's ToS

tools.name: XXMI Launcher
engines: Unity/UE anime games it supports (Genshin, HSR, ZZZ, WuWa, ... see its README)
evidence: %RF_TOOLS%\xxmi (XXMI 2.2.1 + ZZMI 1.5.0 used for the 3 ZZZ frames)
%RF_TOOLS%\zzz-capture-unpack-toolkit

local.note: RF_TOOLS points at a local tool directory; set it before running doctor.

tools.notes: Per-game 3DMigoto packages + injection management. Upstream is far ahead (2.4.9). Capture procedure (Hunting, F8 per frame) is written in the user's toolkit README. Capture tool, not an extractor and not a mod tool by itself.

tools.name: WWMI-Tools (Blender add-on)
tools.notes: Game-specific: reads WuWa frame dumps into Blender with Kuro's buffer layouts (also does mod export). Use its layout knowledge/ output as an alternative WuWa ingest; do NOT treat as generic. Blender is installed locally (D:\Blender) but this add-on was not run.

tools.name: GIMI / SRMI (Genshin / HSR model importers)
tools.notes: MOD tools: they replace assets at runtime. Not an extraction pipeline. Value for us: documented per-game buffer/shader conventions and 3DMigoto config. SR-Model-Importer is stale (2023) and superseded by XXMI's SRMI package.

tools.name: 3DMigoto usage guide (t1ktak)
tools.notes: Documentation for the frame-analysis workflow.

tools.name: UnityPy
evidence: scripts/verify_unitypy.py on a Unity 6 AssetBundle (Texture2D->PNG, Mesh->OBJ, Transform read)
Endfield globalgamemanagers -> Unity 2021.3.34f5 (real game file)
tools.notes: First choice for scripted reading of standard Unity data. Game-specific encryption (custom bundle headers / VFS) must be undone before it can open the data.
risks: no help with encrypted game containers
IL2CPP MonoBehaviours need type info (see il2cppdumper)

tools.name: AssetRipper
evidence: tools/AssetRipper/2.0.0; exported bundle -> Unity project with prefab/mesh/material/png (workspace/verify_unity/assetripper)
tools.notes: Reconstructs a whole Unity project (prefabs, scenes, materials) - best for scene-level recovery when data is readable. GPL-3.0: run it as a separate process (as done here), do not link.

tools.name: AssetStudio (Razviar update branch)
tools.notes: Maintained successor of Perfare/AssetStudio (archived 2022). CLI export of meshes/FBX/textures. Not run; UnityPy + AssetRipper cover the same ground for now.

tools.name: AnimeStudio (ZZZStudio family)
formats: HoYo custom blocks with CAB map
evidence: %RF_TOOLS%\anime-studio (ZZZ 3.2.0)
%RF_TOOLS%\zzz-source-assets (FBX/EXR/animation exported from the installed game)

local.note: RF_TOOLS points at a local tool directory; set it before running doctor.

tools.notes: NOT in the original candidate list but required: HoYo games use custom block formats that generic Unity tools cannot read. This is the model for a per-game 'source adapter'. ZZZ itself is not installed on this machine now, so it was not re-run.
risks: needs the matching installed game version + CAB map

tools.name: UABEA (Unity Asset Bundle Extractor Avalonia)
tools.notes: Bundle inspection/patching GUI. Cannot be scripted; keep as the human fallback for odd bundles.

tools.name: Il2CppDumper / Il2CppInspectorRedux
tools.notes: Recovers type/field layouts from global-metadata.dat + GameAssembly.dll so MonoBehaviour data (scene settings, custom components) can be decoded. Il2CppDumper is stale (2024); LukeFZ/Il2CppInspectorRedux (AGPL-3.0, 2026) is the maintained alternative. Needed for Endfield-class games; not run.

tools.name: CUE4Parse
evidence: <local project>\05_pipeline\source_probe (SourceProbe CLI on CUE4Parse 1.2.2.202609; WuWa 2.1M files indexed, meshes -> GLB, FastGeo layouts)
re-run here: SourceProbe selftest; dump-index of 6,009 LiNaXiTa packages -> 40,958 source sections (52 packages without render data)

local.note: RF_TOOLS points at a local tool directory; set it before running doctor.

tools.notes: The right batch tool for Unreal source assets. Needs the game's AES key (user's SourceProbe reads it from an existing local file; RenderForge never stores or prints keys) and sometimes .usmap mappings.
risks: per-game engine version / AES key / mappings
FastGeo and other UE5 world-partition formats need dedicated handling (user's `layout` command)

tools.name: FModel
tools.notes: Interactive browser/exporter built on CUE4Parse. Use to explore a game by hand and to learn paths/keys; do batch work through CUE4Parse directly. GPL-3.0 - separate process only.

tools.name: UE Python Editor Scripting
evidence: renderforge/ue_scripts/import_scene.py: 523 meshes / 19k instances / 197 materials in ~45 s headless
tools.notes: See CLAUDE.md for the verified pitfalls (StaticMesh creation, ISM via Blueprint, no normal setter, game-mode screenshots).

tools.name: UE Interchange
evidence: 270 PNG textures imported through it (LogInterchangeEngine) in headless runs
tools.notes: Textures verified. Mesh import from glTF/FBX (e.g. CUE4Parse GLB output) not yet exercised: current emitter builds StaticMeshes directly from raw arrays, which avoids FBX/glTF round trips but loses nothing we need yet.

tools.name: Unreal MCP (official, UE 5.8)
evidence: renderforge/httpmcp.py: enumerated ~15 editor toolsets (actor, asset, material, scene, blueprint ...), loaded the reconstructed level, find_actors returned RF_ actors
tools.notes: Enable plugins ModelContextProtocol + ToolsetRegistry + EditorToolset and set bAutoStartServer in DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini (done in ue_project). Experimental / NoRedist plugin. Gives a chat-driven way to inspect and edit the reconstructed level.

tools.name: funplay-unreal-mcp
tools.notes: Alternative to the official MCP (execute_python, PIE automation). Not installed: the official server already covers editing, and headless python covers batch import. Revisit if the official toolsets lack screenshot / PIE control.

tools.name: funplay-unity-mcp
tools.notes: Chat-driven Unity editing. Not installed. The user's environment already exposes a Unity CLI / MCP ('unity' server) and Unity.exe batchmode is verified here.

tools.name: Unity Editor batchmode + Unity CLI
evidence: renderforge/unity_run.py + unity_project/RenderForgeUnity/Assets/Editor/RFImportScene.cs: 523 meshes / 19k instances / textured scene + camera render PNG
tools.notes: First run of a fresh project only imports; run the method twice (or open once) so scripts compile.

tools.name: RDC2UE
evidence: refs/RDC2UE (cloned)
tools.notes: No licence file: do not copy code. Useful ideas: manual ViewProj entry as fallback when auto-detect fails; shader transcription via DXBC decompiler + spirv-cross for material recovery. Game-specific by its own statement.

tools.name: UE5_RenderDoc_To_OBJ
tools.notes: CSV mesh export -> OBJ with UE5 view-buffer reconstruction. No licence file. Our solver (fit local->clip, pick VP from cbuffers) covers the same ground generically.

tools.name: RenderForge rd_extract (RenderDoc -> Extract Package)
evidence: workspace/wuwa_bridge/export (681 opaque scene-pass draws)
workspace/wuwa_bridge/export_transparent4 (67 translucent-pass draws; writes_extra / ps view format recorded)
workspace/wuwa_bridge/export_depth (714 depth-only draws)
workspace/wuwa_61250/ids (2,302 draws, index list only, no geometry export)
tools.notes: D3D11 verified; D3D12/Vulkan code paths use the same API but are unverified. Modes: survey | export | ids. export options: --no-instanced-index, save_rt_inputs (force-save render-target inputs as PNG, e.g. scene colour for a translucent pass), per-draw ownIndices when a mesh shares its index buffer.

tools.name: RenderForge 3DMigoto Frame Analysis ingest
evidence: ZZZ Frame01: 229 DrawIndexed + 61 indirect parsed -> 213 draws / 167 meshes / 83 textures in 6 s
docs/milestone_zzz_3dmigoto_unity.png (Unity), UE render also produced
workspace/zzz_frame01
tools.notes: Parses log.txt + per-draw .buf/.txt/.dds. GPU-driven DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect (ZZZ characters) has GPU-written args that are not in the dump: resolving them from CPU-side update dumps was tried and shreds meshes, so the whole dumped index buffer is used (head/face parts of the ZZZ test character come out missing/merged). Known limitation, root cause identified.

tools.name: RenderForge solver / scene builder
evidence: VP found in 97% of static draws; camera matches reference in UE and Unity
workspace/wuwa_bridge/build: 73 translucent-pass instances placed with affine fits; water draw identified as SM_Old_Wat_08AH
tools.notes: Requires post-VS data (RenderDoc). 3DMigoto path uses build_model_space (identity placement + optional basis). Extra pass merge (--extra-export/--extra-pass) adds a second extract with its own root; billboard/camera-facing quads are rejected (not rigid) rather than baked.

tools.name: RenderForge asset identity (whole-library)
evidence: workspace/wuwa_61250/draw_identity.json: 592/1017 scene-pass draws, 43,336/44,757 instances (96.8%) carry the source asset name from a whole-library index of 157,691 source sections; 469 meshes named
workspace/wuwa_bridge/draw_identity.json: 386/681 draws, 27,727/28,823 instances (96.2%); re-imported to UE and Unity, screenshots re-rendered
SourceProbe dump-index validated against 6 independently matched frame-61250 events (same source object, LOD and section)
whole-frame draw scan (ids mode, 2,302 draws) -> 1,296 matched, no conflicting duplicate-token assignments
tools.notes: Per-draw exact ordered-index SHA-256 against a SourceProbe dump-index of source LOD sections. Full-mesh only: a draw whose index list is a sub-range of a larger source section stays unmatched (no approximation). Duplicate index tokens across draws resolved to one source in this data.

evidence: workspace/wuwa_bridge/shots/compare.png
tools.notes: Accepts scene packages from any source space: converts Unity-space packages to UE space first (renderforge/space.py; vertex round-trip error <1e-6 on a synthetic hierarchy). Material kinds: opaque masked, translucent (alpha), translucent-luminance (BC1 sheets without alpha), water preview (translucent teal tint + captured normal). Near-camera translucent FX hidden by default.

evidence: docs/milestone_unity_target_wuwa_bridge.png

tools.notes: UE: game-mode HighResShot off-screen. Unity: camera render in the import method. Comparison is side-by-side, not a pixel metric yet.

tools.name: SourceProbe (user's CUE4Parse CLI)

local.note: RF_TOOLS points at a local tool directory; set it before running doctor.

tools.notes: Owned by the user's WuWa project; referenced by path, not copied. Writes only under that project's 03_source_assets / 99_scratch. RenderForge added the batch `dump-index` command (per-section hashes + per-LOD index bytes); 41,133 SM_ packages -> 157,691 sections in ~25 min.

tools.name: RenderForge Unity-source ingest (UnityPy -> Scene Package)
evidence: unity_project/RenderForgeUnity/Bundles/rftest: Transform hierarchy world matrices match Unity's own localToWorldMatrix to 1.6e-7; asymmetric wedge mesh vertices exact; textured scene rendered in Unity and imported into UE
tools.notes: Source-only route: no GPU capture involved. Handles Transform hierarchy, MeshFilter+MeshRenderer, Mesh (raw arrays via UnityPy MeshHandler), Material main/bump textures. Not yet exercised on a commercial game (none with readable bundles available locally); skinned meshes, LODGroups, prefab variants and scene files are not handled.

tools.name: RenderForge space converter (ue <-> unity)
evidence: numeric check: world-space vertices identical after unity->ue conversion (8.6e-7 cm)
same RenderDoc scene rendered with correct camera in both engines
tools.notes: Handles axis permutation + unit scale, instance matrices, normals, camera. Winding is preserved (both are left-handed). UV V-flip is done by the Unity emitter only.

tools.name: RenderForge workbench (case status + resumable step graph)
evidence: workspace/*/case.json: every case carries steps.<name> (time, numbers) after run
wuwa_f3422: stale UE import detected by cross-checking the UE project, re-imported and re-shot
wuwa_f3765: 19-draw legacy case taken from export to metrics in one `run` (39 s)
tools.notes: A stage is done only when its artifact exists on disk; a recorded import is cross-checked against the engine project. Steps that need input not on disk (identify index, capture path) are skipped with the reason. Build options that change the result (extra_export/extra_pass) persist in case.json and are reused on rebuild.

tools.name: RenderForge numeric comparison (SSIM / error / coverage)
evidence: workspace/*/metrics.json for wuwa_bridge (UE 0.322 / Unity 0.349 SSIM), wuwa_61250 (0.393), wuwa_f3765 (0.533), zzz_frame01 (0.212)
orientation detection flips zzz_frame01 (stored bottom-up) and leaves the others as-is
tools.notes: Approximate same-viewpoint comparison, not pixel-identical. SSIM on BT.601 luminance (integral images), MAE/RMSE/p95, foreground-coverage error, mask IoU. ~1.1 s per 1080p pair.

tools.name: RenderForge offline regression fixture
evidence: 6 checks in ~4 s: space round-trip (0 vertex error), Unity ingest vs localToWorldMatrix (1.6e-7), scene integrity, metrics self-consistency + flip, case scan, toolbox data
tools.notes: No GPU / RenderDoc / UE / Unity needed; covers committed fixtures only. Exit 1 on failure.

tools.name: RenderForge MCP server (stdio) + background jobs
evidence: scripted stdio client: doctor/plan/games/status/metrics/step/job_start/job_status/job_log all returned JSON; job_start ran a full case in the background (39 s, exit 0)
tools.notes: Standard library only; tools are thin wrappers over the CLI so output is identical. job_start writes workspace/_jobs/<id>.log plus an exit marker, so a later session can still read the outcome. Not yet exercised from a fresh Claude session through the harness.

tools.name: RenderForge workbench asset export (OBJ / GLB / texture / case zip)
evidence: scripts/dev/web_acceptance.py export-glb-well-formed / export-obj-faces / export-case-zip / export-job-* (42/42)
workspace/_exports/*.zip: 535-mesh case subsets written by export_job and re-opened with zipfile
tools.notes: Derived from build/scene.json alone: no re-solving, no invented geometry. GLB is a single mesh per file with positional/normal/UV accessors (uint32 indices above 65535 vertices) and keeps the package top-left UV origin; OBJ flips V because OBJ is bottom-left. Whole-case zips ship scene.json verbatim, INSTANCES.csv, CAMERA.json, REPORT.md and the textures the exported meshes reference. Large cases run as a child process (renderforge.web.export_job) so the HTTP threads stay free. Materials are preview level, not the game shaders.
